item.title: Arinkin's sheaf and Hilbert schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.26699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arinkin's sheaf gives a relative Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence of a general Beauville-Mukai system, extending the usual Poincar\'e bundle over the smooth locus. We provide an alternative construction of it as a deformation of the Fourier-Mukai autoequivalence on the Hilbert scheme of an elliptic K3 surface obtained by lifting the classical Poincar\'e kernel for an elliptic surface. As applications, we show that the $P=C$ property for a general Beauville-Mukai system is equivalent to that for the Hilbert scheme fibration, thus providing new proofs for both. We also construct an explicit deformation that connects Markman's construction of a projectively hyperholomorphic bundle on products of hyper-K\"ahler manifolds of K3${}^{[g]}$-type to that of Hartlieb and Shah. This answers a question of Hartlieb and Shah.
item.dc:creator: David Zhiyuan Bai

item.title: Opposite filtrations on the parabolic compactified Jacobian
item.description: arXiv:2611.26789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Hikita filtration on the cohomology of the parabolic compactified Jacobian of the plane curve singularity $x^m=y^n$, $(m,n)=1$, is opposite to the perverse filtration in a precise sense. This implies the parabolic Hilb-vs-Quot conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19633, and consequently the main conjecture from https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.2115 for these singularities. The new ingredient is an analysis of how the Bott-Mitchell filtration on the homology of the affine Grassmannian of $SL_n$ relates to both of the above filtrations.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Kivinen

item.title: Tensor products of additive groups as reciprocity sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2611.26947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Nisnevich reciprocity sheaves associated with tensor products of the cube-invariant objects for the additive and multiplicative groups, with at least one additive factor. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, these sheaves decompose into direct sums of absolute K$\"a$hler differential sheaves with binomial multiplicities. As an application, we compute the associated reciprocity sheaves of the Hochschild homology of the additive object.
item.dc:creator: Toshiro Hiranouchi, Rin Sugiyama

item.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
item.description: arXiv:2611.26974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.
item.dc:creator: Yang-Hui He

item.title: Period maps and the $C_{\rm st}$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.27054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a family of elliptic curves over an open disc whose total space violates the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture in degree $1$. Hence the conjecture, known for proper and for Stein varieties, as well as for products of such, does not extend to proper families over Stein bases. This is an instance of a general criterion: the $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ conjecture holds for the total space of a smooth proper family over a sufficiently small open disc if and only if its period map is constant, i.e., all Gauss--Manin Higgs fields vanish or, equivalently, the $p$-adic local systems $R^if_*\mathbf{Q}_p$ are geometrically constant. This criterion is special to curves: over a $2$-dimensional polydisc, we give a family of $p$-adic analogues of non-K\"ahler elliptic surfaces whose period maps and local systems are constant, but whose total space violates the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Colmez, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}, Xinyu Shao

item.title: Demazure-Lusztig type operators and correspondences on Kato Catalan varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.27081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the integral equivariant cohomology rings of Kato Catalan varieties $\mathscr{X}_\Psi$ associated with arbitrary root ideals $\Psi$ in type $A$. These varieties are smooth projective compactifications of the vector subbundles $T^*_\Psi\mathcal{B}$ of the cotangent bundle of the complete flag variety $\mathcal{B}$. Let $K$ denote the product of the general linear group (or its maximal torus) with the loop rotation torus $\mathbb{C}^\times$. We give an explicit presentation of $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_\Psi;\mathbb{Z})$ with relations expressed in terms of divided difference and Demazure-Lusztig type operators. Furthermore, for every simple reflection preserving $\Psi\cup(-\Psi)$, we construct a geometric realization of the associated Demazure-Lusztig type operator on $H^*_K(\mathscr{X}_\Psi;\mathbb{Z})$ via correspondences. These correspondences yield a faithful graded action of the subalgebra of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra generated by these reflections and the polynomial subalgebra. For the maximal root ideal $\Psi=\Delta^+$, our construction recovers the cohomological counterpart of the $K$-theoretic Steinberg correspondences of Cautis and Kamnitzer.
item.dc:creator: Taiyo Kodama

item.title: Combinatorial relative orientability for toric and tropical geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.27238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many problems in enumerative geometry are solved by computing the degree of the top Chern class of a suitable vector bundle. Results from $\mathbb{A}^1$-homotopy theory allow to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields, replacing the top Chern class by the Euler class in Chow-Witt groups. For its degree to be well-defined, one needs the vector bundle to be relatively oriented. Another way to solve enumerative problems is to translate them to tropical geometry, where they become combinatorial problems. In this paper, we give a combinatorial description of relative orientability for vector bundles over smooth proper toric varieties. We show that it behaves well under tropicalization, establishing a tropical version of relative orientability, which will allow to the use of tropical geometry to answer enumerative questions over arbitrary fields. As a demonstration, we prove a quadratically enriched version of the Bernstein-Khovanskii-Kushnirenko theorem via tropical geometry. Lastly, we define the notion of $k$-phase structures on tropical hypersurfaces, generalizing the real case.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Tiggemann

item.title: Chern classes, Poincar\'e polynomials, and Bernstein-Sato polynomials of plane curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.27297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Poincar\'e polynomial of a reduced plane curve $C$ is the Chern polynomial of the dual of the bundle of Jacobian syzygies of $C$. Using the Zeuthen-Segre formula, we prove that its value at $t=-1$ equals the Euler number of the complement of $C$ up to the correction term $\mu(C)-\tau(C)$, so the two numbers coincide if and only if all singularities of $C$ are quasi-homogeneous. As applications, we show that the defect in a combinatorial inequality for free $d$-arrangements is the square of the difference of the exponents, extend the addition technique to arbitrary reduced plane curves, and locate the roots of local Bernstein-Sato polynomials at ordinary singular points.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Pokora

item.title: An affine surface with 3-step nilpotent fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2611.27475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth complex affine surface $Y$ such that $\pi_1(Y)$ is virtually $3$-step nilpotent, but not virtually $2$-step nilpotent. This gives a negative answer to the quasi-projective version of Campana's nilpotency problem.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Polevoy, Vasily Rogov

item.title: Classification of strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure surface singularities with imperfect residue fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.27597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study strongly $F$-regular and $F$-pure normal surface singularities whose residue fields are not necessarily perfect. We characterize strong $F$-regularity in terms of the weighted dual graph and geometric reducedness of the exceptional components of the minimal resolution, extending Hara's classification over algebraically closed residue fields. We also determine the possible dual graphs of $F$-pure surface singularities and give converse criteria. Notably, the exceptional components of an $F$-pure surface singularity are geometrically reduced unless the singularity is a rational double point.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuro Kawakami, Kenta Sato

item.title: Projectivized ASEP-Bethe system and counting solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of counting solutions to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equations. In an earlier preprint, Brattain, Do, and Saenz presented an algebro-geometric method for counting the number of such solutions. As their method relies on sophisticated machinery, it requires advanced knowledge of algebraic geometry and topology. In this paper, we provide an alternative and simpler method for counting solutions, based on a standard intersection theory on projective varieties. We take a conventional approach in algebraic geometry: ``Projectivize the problem and count degrees.'' We introduce a projectivized version of the ASEP-Bethe equations, whose solution set is realized as a subscheme of a certain projective variety. Varying the hopping-rate parameter $p$, we give a one-parameter family $S$ of the solution sets. We show that, for the ASEP with $n$ sites and $m$ particles, the fiber $S|_p$ with generic $p$ contains $\binom{n}{m}$ points with multiplicity, which equals the expected number of admissible Bethe roots to the ASEP-Bethe ansatz equation.
item.dc:creator: Shinsuke Iwao

item.title: Calabi-Yau fibrations and orbifold Mordell
item.description: arXiv:2611.27727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct isotrivial projective families of Calabi-Yau varieties with arbitrarily large inf-multiplicities and no divisible fibres over the projective line. As an application, we show that any single instance of Campana's Orbifold Mordell Conjecture for a general-type C-pair of genus at most one (with only finite multiplicities) implies that the Weakly Special Conjecture is false.
item.dc:creator: Ariyan Javanpeykar

item.title: Incidence Correspondences and Chow Motives in the Symplectic (Z/2Z)4-K3 Locus
item.description: arXiv:2611.27800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Chow-motivic framework for projective K3 surfaces with a symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action. For the universal Heisenberg-invariant quartic family, we show that the generically defined codimension-two cycles on the relative square are generated by three ambient classes and sixteen automorphism graphs, and that these nineteen classes are cohomologically independent. Combining this square-Franchetta property with a finite-cover trace construction and the Kuga-Satake correspondence, we prove that every smooth Heisenberg-invariant quartic K3 surface has a Chow motive of abelian type. We also consider the diagonal complete-intersection family of three quadrics and establish stability of the Heisenberg result under rational Hodge isogenies. For arbitrary projective K3 surfaces with a faithful symplectic (Z/2Z)^4-action, we obtain a motivic reduction to the minimal resolution of the fifteen-node quotient. Applying a rational Kuga-Satake criterion, we establish abelianity of Chow motives for explicit infinite arithmetic subfamilies of all three Garbagnati-Sarti lattice types, including their Picard-rank specializations. Finally, we prove a square-Franchetta theorem for the ten-dimensional family of double-cubic K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Sixuan Gu

item.title: Kneser-Tits over fields of cohomological dimension $\le 2$ (with an appendix by Alexis Bouthier and Federico Scavia)
item.description: arXiv:2611.27803v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We settle the Kneser-Tits problem over every field $k$ of (separable) cohomological dimension $\le 2$, thus resolving a conjecture of Gille. More precisely, for such a $k$ and a semisimple, simply connected $k$-group $G$ whose indecomposable factors over $k$ are isotropic, we show that $G(k)$ is generated by "elementary matrices" (the $k$-points of the unipotent radicals of the parabolic $k$-subgroups of $G$), in other words, that $K_1^G(k) \cong 1$. In fact, we show this vanishing already when $k$ has separable $p$-dimension $\le 2$ in the sense of Gille with respect to a subset of the torsion primes $p$ of $G$, and we reinterpret the separable $p$-dimension itself via syntomic cohomology. To approach those $G$ that escape the net of previously known cases, for an inclusion of reductive $k$-groups $M \subset L$, we develop a new method based on the Rost invariant for transferring $R$-equivalence on $L/M$ to $R$-equivalence on $L$. To find homogeneous spaces to which our method fruitfully applies, we use the theories of prehomogeneous vector spaces and of special symplectic representations: concretely, for a $32$-dimensional half-spin representation $V$, we argue that the vectors in its unique open orbit $O \subset V$ admit unique up to interchange decompositions into sums of two pure spinors, and show that various double covers of $O$ built from such decompositions are rational varieties over any base field.
item.dc:creator: Kestutis Cesnavicius

item.title: Elementary length of polynomial automorphisms in dimension at least three
item.description: arXiv:2611.27840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the plane the number and the degrees of the de Jonqui\`eres letters in a reduced word of a polynomial automorphism are invariants. For $n\ge3$ we study how much of a decomposition of an automorphism $F$ of $K^n$ into elementary maps can be recovered from $F$. Let $\Gamma(K,n)$ be the group of tame automorphisms of $K^n$ with Jacobian determinant $1$, which is generated by the elementary maps, and let $\ell(F)$ be the least number of elementary factors of $F\in\Gamma(K,n)$. The decompositions of length $\#\operatorname{supp}(F)$, the number of coordinates moved by $F$, are exactly those obtained by successive extraction of left elementary factors, which are determined by $F^{-1}$. Decompositions of length $\#\operatorname{supp}(F)+1$ reduce to this case up to one unknown tail, and $\ell(F\times\mathrm{Id}_{K^r})=\ell(F)$ whenever $\ell(F)\le\#\operatorname{supp}(F)+2$. Vasyunin's quadratic automorphism of $K^5$, $\mathrm{char}\,K\ne2$, has exactly six minimal decompositions, of length $4$, which differ in the degrees of their factors. Its dynamical degree is $\sqrt2$, and in characteristic zero its iterates $F^{(m)}$, $m\ge2$, satisfy $5\le\ell(F^{(m)})\le4m$. In characteristic zero the automorphisms of $K^3$ in the normal form of He and Yan satisfy $\ell(F)=\#\operatorname{supp}(F)+1$, and their minimal decompositions form two classes up to natural moves. Together with the classification of Wang and Yan this shows that a map $X+H$ of $K^3$ with $H(0)=0$ and nilpotent $J_H$ is Pascal finite if and only if the components of $H$ are linearly dependent. The Anick automorphism $A$ of $K^4$ satisfies $\ell(A)\ge\#\operatorname{supp}(A)+4=6$ over every field over which $A\in\Gamma(K,4)$, $\ell(A)\le16$ if $\mathrm{char}\,K\ne2$, and $\ell(A\times\mathrm{Id}_K)\le6$ over every field.\ell(A\times\Id_K)\le6$ over every field.
item.dc:creator: El\.zbieta Adamus, Zbigniew Hajto

item.title: H\"older continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.27974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally H\"older continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a H\"older saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose H\"older saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the H\"older saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-H\"older homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-H\"older homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative H\"older saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, H\"older equisingularity, defined by a bi-H\"older trivialization, and the stronger H\"older equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Bernard, Antoni Rangachev

item.title: Feynman integrals, coactions and Lie-algebra representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.26679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We outline a link between canonical differential equations of Feynman integrals and matrix representations of flat connections taking values in certain Lie algebras. Leveraging insights from string theory and properties of periods associated with these Lie algebras, we deduce single-valued solutions to the differential equations and coactions for the integrals. We introduce a novel form of the differential equations which connects with the representation theory of the Lie algebras and may depart from $\varepsilon$-factorisation in a controlled way. We illustrate the formalism through relevant examples.
item.dc:creator: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr, Axel Kleinschmidt, Franca Lippert, Oliver Schlotterer, Yoann Sohnle

item.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.26750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $\xi$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.
item.dc:creator: Cass Halleck-Dub\'e

item.title: Constructing toric diagonal modules with short linear resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.27025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a complete simplicial toric variety $X$, we construct a collection of Cohen--Macaulay modules with linear resolutions where the associated sheaf is the diagonal. Through this work, we see that the resolutions constructed by Favero--Huang from homotopy path algebras and those constructed by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev can be viewed as two dual methods to construct resolutions of the diagonal starting from a compatible $\mathbb{Z}^n$-stratification.
item.dc:creator: Jay Yang

item.title: An explicit Cassels--Tate pairing in characteristic $2$ and the parity of $2$-Selmer ranks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a global field of characteristic $2$ and $\varphi\colon E\to E'$ the Verschiebung of an ordinary elliptic curve $E/K$ with a rational point of order $2$. We prove an explicit formula for the homogeneous-space Cassels--Tate pairing on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$ as a sum of local Artin--Schreier symbols, show that it coincides with Kramer's descent pairing and, on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]$, with the pairing induced by Milne's flat duality, and deduce that it is non-degenerate on $\Sha(E/K)[\varphi]/\hat\varphi(\Sha(E'/K)[2])$. For every ordinary elliptic curve $A/K$ we express the parity of $\mathrm{rk}\,A(K)+\dim\Sha(A/K)[2]$ by local terms (after Kramer), and identify these with local root numbers at places of semistable or potentially multiplicative reduction, and in further cases using curves with finite $\Sha$. We determine $\Sha$ in examples, and extend the formula to rational points of any prime order $\ell$, the new case being $\ell=\operatorname{char}K$.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Shukla

item.title: Nonreduced Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c Schubert schemes
item.description: arXiv:2611.27130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an effective numerical criterion ($\theta$-minimality) to detect the nonreducedness of Finkelberg-Mirkovi\'c (FM) Schubert schemes via tangent-space comparisons at arbitrary torus-fixed points. We completely classify the dominant coweights admitting $\theta$-minimal pairs. As an application, we obtain nonreduced FM Schubert schemes in every type other than $A_n$ and $C_n$. In particular, every nontrivial FM Schubert scheme of type $E_8$ is nonreduced. In type $D_n$, we show that some nonreduced FM Schubert schemes and their corresponding spherical Schubert varieties have the same tangent space at the base point. Our methods use the Frenkel-Kac construction of basic representations and Segal-Sugawara operators.
item.dc:creator: Marc Besson, Jiuzu Hong, Huanhuan Yu

item.title: Splitting types of Richelot isogenies over finite fields and a newform of weight four
item.description: arXiv:2611.27775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A factorization $f=uvw$ of a square-free sextic over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ of odd characteristic into three monic quadratics defines a genus-2 curve with a rational $(2,2)$-isogeny kernel, and the Richelot construction attaches to it three dual quadratics $U,V,W$. We determine, for every odd prime power $q$, the number of such factorizations with prescribed splitting behaviour over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of all six quadratics. Each of the $64$ counts is $q(q-1)(q+1-n_f)/64$ times $C(q)\pm t_q$, where $n_f$ is the number of roots of $f$ in $\mathbb{F}_q$, $C$ is an explicit monic cubic, and $t_q$ is the trace of Frobenius attached to the newform $\eta(2z)^{4}\eta(4z)^{4}$ of weight $4$ and level $8$. The proof reduces the counts by elementary means to a twisted second moment of the Legendre family of elliptic curves, which is a value of a hypergeometric function over $\mathbb{F}_q$ evaluated by Ahlgren and Ono for primes. As consequences, the number of factorizations whose three pairwise resultants lie in one square class is a polynomial in $q$, with proportion $1/4+3/(4q^{2})+O(q^{-4})$. When the quotient is a product of two elliptic curves conjugate over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$, we prove that the splitting of the factors $u,v,w$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ decides which points of order two of the elliptic factor are divisible by two.
item.dc:creator: Hung Dang

item.title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
item.description: arXiv:2611.27861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.
item.dc:creator: Rak-Kyeong Seong

item.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.27879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $\pi_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class of solid rings in characteristic $p$.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Barthel, Lucas Mann, Rin Ray, Tomer M. Schlank, Andrew Senger, Jared Weinstein, Xinyu Zhou

item.title: Euler characteristics and moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2306.06343v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fujiki--Oka resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities of type $\frac{1}{r}(1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)$ are constructed using multidimensional continued fractions. In this paper, we compute the Euler characteristics of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in arbitrary dimension using the heights of the coefficients of the associated remainder polynomials. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in dimension three.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Sato

item.title: Categorical concentration
item.description: arXiv:2308.01652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a torus action on a compact space $X$, a fundamental result of Borel and Atiyah-Segal asserts that the equivariant cohomology of $X$ is concentrated in the fixed locus $X^T$, up to inverting enough Chern classes. For algebraic varieties and stacks over an arbitrary field, we prove an analogous concentration statement for equivariant derived categories of sheaves. On the localized categories, restriction to the fixed locus coincides with Braden's hyperbolic localization, and as an application we obtain torus localization for the Donaldson-Thomas perverse sheaves of (-1)-shifted symplectic spaces. Concentration holds more generally for actions of affine algebraic groups, and for abstract six functor formalisms (e.g. motivic sheaves). For $\mu_\ell$-actions, it recovers Treumann's sheaf-theoretic Smith theory. We also prove a categorification of the virtual localization formula for torus actions.
item.dc:creator: Adeel A. Khan, Charanya Ravi

item.title: On the Unipotent $p$-adic Simpson Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2403.04565v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this paper is to show a (derived) $p$-adic Simpson correspondence for (locally) unipotent coefficients on smooth rigid-analytic varieties. Our results depend on a deformation to $\mathbf{B}_\mathtt{dr}^+/\xi^2$, and not on a choice of exponential (as required for more general coefficients). Our methods are higher categorical, hinging on the theory of modules over $\mathbf{E}_\infty$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Thiago Solovera e Nery

item.title: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2503.23382v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.
item.dc:creator: Mohan Bhupal, Sergey Finashin

item.title: Solvable points on intersections of quadrics, cubics, and quartics
item.description: arXiv:2508.00215v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not 2 or 3. We establish polynomial bounds on the ambient dimension $N$, such that if $N$ is at least as big as this bound, every intersection $X\subset\mathbb{P}^N$ of quadrics, cubics and quartics has a solvable point, and a general one has a dense collection of solvable points, i.e. points in $X(k^{\mathrm{Sol}})$ where $k^{\mathrm{Sol}}/k$ is a solvable closure. Our method connects the classical theory of polar hypersurfaces to Fano varieties $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$ of linear subspaces on $X$, and we use this to obtain improved control on the arithmetic of $\mathcal{F}(j,X)$
item.dc:creator: Claudio G\'omez-Gonz\'ales, Jesse Wolfson

item.title: Defect of projective hypersurfaces with isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2512.23522v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a hypersurface with isolated singularities defined by $f$ in ${\bf P^{n+1}}$ with $n>1$. The difference ${\rm def}(X):=h^{n+1}(X)-h^{n-1}(X)$ is called the defect of $X$ (for self-duality of the cohomology of $X$). It is known that its vanishing is closely related to ${\bf Q}$-factoriality of $X$ without assuming rational singularities when $n=3$. This number coincides with the dimension of the cokernel of the inclusion $H^{n-1}(X)\to{\rm IH}^{n-1}(X)$, the rank of the morphism from the vanishing cohomologies of $X$ to $H^{n+1}(X)$ for a one-parameter smoothing of $X$ with total space smooth, and also with the dimension of the unipotent monodromy part of the Milnor fiber cohomology of $f$ with degree $n$. In the case $X$ has only weighted homogeneous isolated singularities, the defect ${\rm def}(X)$ is then given by the $E_2$-term of the spectral sequence of the double complex with differentials ${\rm d}f\wedge$ and $\rm d$ by the $E_2$-degeneration of the pole order spectral sequence. It can be calculated explicitly using a computer even for analogues of the Hirzebruch quintic threefold with more than one hundred ordinary double points found by B.\ van Geemen and J.\ Werner in a compatible way with their computation. We give also an example with ${\rm def}(X)>0$ and $|{\rm Sing}\,X|=1$ in the non-projective cone case where $n=3$.
item.dc:creator: Seung-Jo Jung, Morihiko Saito

item.title: Components of the nested Hilbert scheme of few points
item.description: arXiv:2601.16765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the existence and the schematic structure of elementary components of the nested Hilbert scheme on a smooth quasi-projective variety. More precisely, we establish a new lower bound for the existence of non-smoothable nestings of fat points on a smooth $n$-fold, for $n\geqslant 4$. Moreover, we develop a systematic method for building generically non-reduced elementary components. We also investigate the irreducibility of the Hilbert scheme of points on a singular hypersurface of $\mathbb A^3$. Explicitly, we show that the Hilbert scheme of points on a hypersurface of $\mathbb{A}^3$ having a singularity of multiplicity at least 5 admits elementary components.
item.dc:creator: Michele Graffeo, Paolo Lella

item.title: Higher rank bundles on Hopf surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.06936v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of filtrable stable bundles on the Hopf surface with any rank and $c_2>0$, and show they must have jumps.In the opposite direction, for each integer $r\ge 2$ we prove the existence of irreducible rank $r$ vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant, $c_2=1$, and no jumps. We apply codimension $2$ operations to elements of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{r,n}$ of rank $r$ stable vector bundles with $c_2=n$ on the Hopf surface, obtaining families of torsion free sheaves in the closure of $\mathcal M_{r,n+1}$ when $c_2>1$.
item.dc:creator: Edoardo Ballico, Elizabeth Gasparim

item.title: On the Generalized Arithmetic Picard--Lefschetz Formula
item.description: arXiv:2607.05757v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper establishes an explicit arithmetic Picard--Lefschetz formula for isolated singularities of diagonal type. We investigate proper flat families of varieties over a henselian discrete valuation ring whose fraction field has characteristic zero. When the smooth generic fibre degenerates into a special fibre with isolated diagonal singularities, we construct an explicit eigenbasis for the tame inertia action on the local cohomology and obtain formulas for the intersection pairing and the variation morphism in this basis. When the residue field is finite, we also compute the traces of geometric Frobenius on the inertia invariants in terms of Jacobi sums. We apply this framework to the arithmetic study of symmetric powers of the Airy sheaf. Using geometric realizations associated with Airy moments, we establish specialization exact sequences for compactly supported and middle cohomology and determine the Frobenius characteristic polynomials of inertia-invariant local contributions.
item.dc:creator: Ping-Hsun Chuang

item.title: Fundamental group schemes of globally F-regular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2607.26785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let X be a globally F-regular projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We show that the Nori fundamental group scheme of its regular locus is finite and linearly reductive. Finiteness is the counterpart of theorems of Xu and Braun on the fundamental group of the smooth locus of a complex log Fano variety. The key input is that if a cover of a splinter is a torsor in codimension one and induces an isomorphism on global functions, then its structure group is linearly reductive. We then show that towers of such covers stabilize, both over globally $F$-regular varieties and, in mixed characteristic, over the globally $+$-regular schemes considered by Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker.
item.dc:creator: Charles Vial

item.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
item.description: arXiv:2609.38664v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Chen, Joshua Im, Steven J. Miller, Devayani Pradhan

item.title: Curvature rank, numerical dimension, and cohomology growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.09295v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be the least integer such that the first Bott--Chern class of $L$ is represented by a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form of rank at most $r$ at every point. For any nonzero coherent analytic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ whose support has dimension $d$, we prove that $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $0\le q\le d$. This is the exponent conjectured by Ma--Marinescu--Zelditch, up to an arbitrarily small loss. In the extreme degrees $q=0$ and $q=d,$ the bound can be taken to be $O(p^{\min\{r,d\}})$. If, moreover, $X$ is in Fujiki's class and $L$ is nef, then $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O(p^{\min\{\nu(L),\,d-q\}})$, where $\nu(L)$ is the numerical dimension of $L$. This answers a question of Demailly for compact Fujiki manifolds. Finally, for arbitrary $X$, any singular Hermitian metric \(h\) on \(L\) with semipositive curvature and analytic singularities, and any holomorphic vector bundle \(E\) on $X$, we have \(h^q(X,E\otimes L^p\otimes\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p}))=O_\varepsilon(p^{\min\{n-q,b+\varepsilon\}})\) for any $0\leq q\leq n$, where \(b\) is the maximum curvature rank outside the pole set of $h$, and $\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p})$ is the multiplier ideal sheaf. When $X$ belongs to Fujiki's class, the exponent is \(\min\{n-q,b\}\).
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. To study the converse, we associate to each endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one a family of holonomic $A_2(k)$-modules over finite fields $k$. Kontsevich's conjecture predicts the existence of a $\mathcal D$-module in characteristic zero, unique up to isomorphism, whose reductions to positive characteristic are isomorphic to the prescribed modules. We prove uniqueness whenever such a lift exists. If these lifts exist for every such endomorphism, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge2$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb A^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. We also study an ultraproduct version of the lifting problem: whether these finite-field modules can be recovered as reductions of a single module in characteristic zero along a chosen ultrafilter. We prove that this is possible precisely when the Berest--Wilson invariants of these modules, regarded as left $A_1(k)$-modules, are bounded along that ultrafilter. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Kanel-Belov, Timofey Fedorov

item.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39368v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle. More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic N\'eron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles. For Picard number one and for isotropic N\'eron--Severi lattices of rank two, we further obtain modular-curve criteria for generation by reflective involutions and unipotent isometries, including a complete classification in the split case $N\cong U(d)$.
item.dc:creator: Zaiyuan Chen, Zhiyuan Li

item.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.18317v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Shen

item.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
item.description: arXiv:2611.21108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be the blow-up of a smooth quadric threefold along a twisted quartic, and let $G\subset\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be a finite subgroup such that $\mathrm{Pic}^G(X)$ has rank one. We prove that $X$ is $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. The action of $G$ on $X$ is linearisable if and only if it is projectively linearisable, and this holds precisely when $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Malbon, Antoine Pinardin

item.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
item.description: arXiv:2611.21654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.
item.dc:creator: Takafumi Kouno

item.title: Monodromy groups of Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2303.00804v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field. The connected monodromy field of $A$ is the minimal field over which the images of all the $\ell$-adic torsion representations have connected Zariski closure. We show that for all even $g \geq 4$, there exist infinitely many geometrically nonisogenous abelian varieties $A$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of dimension $g$ where the connected monodromy field is strictly larger than the field of definition of the endomorphisms of $A$. Our construction arises from explicit families of hyperelliptic Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Cantoral-Farf\'an, Davide Lombardo, John Voight

item.title: Reduction by stages for affine W-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2501.04501v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a pair of nilpotent orbits in a simple Lie algebra, one can associate a pair of vertex algebras called affine W-algebras. Under some compatibility conditions on these orbits, we prove that one of these W-algebras can be obtained as the quantum Hamiltonian reduction of the other. This property is called reduction by stages. We provide several examples in classical and exceptional types. To prove reduction by stages for affine W-algebras, we use our previous work on reduction by stages for the Slodowy slices associated with these nilpotent orbits, these slices being the associated varieties of the W-algebras. We also prove and use the fact that each W-algebra can be defined using several equivalent BRST cohomology constructions: choosing the right BRST complexes allows us to connect the two W-algebras in a natural way.
item.dc:creator: Naoki Genra, Thibault Juillard

item.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
item.description: arXiv:2506.02900v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Daw

item.title: Lie Algebra Decomposition Classes for Reductive Algebraic Groups in Arbitrary Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2511.01440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the decomposition classes of the Lie algebras of connected reductive algebraic groups, over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We extend some results proved previously under restrictions on the characteristic, including a formula for the dimension of a decomposition class, and introduce Levi-type decomposition classes to account for some of the difficulties encountered in bad characteristic. We also establish properties of Lusztig--Spaltenstein induction of non-nilpotent orbits, such as parabolic independence, extending the known results for nilpotent orbits. Finally, we determine the covering relation for the closure order on decomposition classes, in the case of good characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Joel Summerfield

item.title: Finite quotients of full surface braid groups and complex surfaces of general type: cyclic, dihedral, and extra-special quotients
item.description: arXiv:2607.18493v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathsf{B}_2(\Sigma_g)$ be the full braid group on two strings on a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We compute the number of epimorphisms $\varphi \colon \mathsf{B}_2(\Sigma_g) \to G$, where $G$ is a finite cyclic, dihedral or extra-special group, under the assumption that $\varphi$ does not factor through $\pi_1(\operatorname{Sym}^2\Sigma_g)$. We then apply our algebraic results to the geometric problem of constructing smooth surfaces of general type as Galois covers of $\operatorname{Sym}^2\Sigma_g$ branched along the diagonal. Notably, when the branching order is at least $3$, we obtain surfaces with positive signature, i.e. $c_1^2>2c_2$. In particular, we construct two $3$-dimensional families of minimal surfaces of general type with $p_g(S)=154$, $q(S)=2$ and $K_S^2=1269$, such that members of different families have the same numerical invariants, the same Betti numbers and the same positive signature, but different torsion subgroups in their first integral homology groups.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano Alessandro, Michelangelo Migliano, Francesco Polizzi

item.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
item.description: arXiv:2610.29889v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].
item.dc:creator: Elke Neuhaus, Irem Portakal, Luca Sodomaco, Katherine Tung

item.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13155v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(N)$ is known for all $N\le 40$ by work of Derickx and van Hoeij. We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ are both $12$. The upper bound $12$ was already known, and we raise the previous lower bound from $10$ to $12$. Since the set of rational points of the Jacobian, $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$, is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces on $X_1(42)$ over $\mathbb F_5$, following Derickx and van Hoeij. We reduce this search by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$. This leaves $743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces, about a quarter of the number needed by the earlier method. We prove the reductions and provide the code and data needed to reproduce the computations.
item.dc:creator: Sourajyoti Maiti
